IR.rationale: A rise in intermediate Treasury yields relative to the policy rate means duration losses and tighter funding. This hits USD EM sovereigns and the rate-sensitive part of high yield, and it may carry forward as yields trend.

B.rationale: Widening spreads together with weak high-yield returns mark a credit sell-off. Illiquid bond indices adjust slowly and then partly revert, so this state carries information about subsequent returns.

V.rationale: High equity implied volatility signals a high price of risk and elevated required credit premia. That predicts subsequent spread compensation and rebounds.

AP.rationale: Stock returns lead corporate and EM bond returns because equity prices impound news about firm value and sovereign risk faster than less liquid bond markets do.

ST.rationale: Momentum losses typically occur when beaten-down, high-beta, levered names rally. Those are risk-on reversals that coincide with junk-credit recoveries.

FX.rationale: Dollar strength together with weakness in a commodity carry currency signals global risk-off and tighter dollar funding. Both weigh on EM sovereign and high-yield credit.

COM.rationale: Energy issuers are a large share of US high yield and many EM sovereigns are oil exporters, so oil price gains improve their credit quality.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions raise risk premia. They forecast both continued credit weakness and higher expected compensation going forward.

ENDG.rationale: High-yield and EM bond index returns show positive short-horizon autocorrelation because of stale pricing and slow information diffusion.

IR.rationale: Sharp rises in intermediate yields signal monetary-policy repricing. This raises the volatility of duration-bearing EM and high-yield bonds.

B.rationale: Credit widening with falling junk prices signals rising default risk and forced selling, which raise subsequent bond-return variance.

V.rationale: Implied volatility is forward-looking. Elevated equity and oil volatility together signal broad risk that spills into credit and commodity-linked issuers.

AP.rationale: The leverage effect means negative equity returns raise future volatility, and credit volatility rises with the volatility of firm assets.

ST.rationale: Momentum crashes occur in turbulent, high-volatility regimes, so momentum losses flag unstable markets.

FX.rationale: Yen appreciation together with Australian-dollar weakness is the signature of a carry unwind and deleveraging. That episode type comes with elevated cross-asset volatility.

COM.rationale: Oil price drops raise distress risk among energy high-yield issuers and oil-exporting sovereigns, which increases their bond-price variance.

MC.rationale: Financial stress indices aggregate spreads, volatility and funding strains, and they predict persistent turbulence.

ENDG.rationale: Volatility clusters, and very high recent variance tends to persist beyond what a simple persistence model captures.

IR.rationale: Rapid rate rises can trigger outflows from EM and high-yield bond funds, producing large duration and spread losses at the same time.

B.rationale: An ongoing credit sell-off raises the chance of continued forced selling and tail losses in illiquid bond markets.

V.rationale: High implied volatility widens the return distribution and signals crash risk in risky credit.

AP.rationale: Emerging-market equity weakness leads EM sovereign and global risk-asset stress, raising the odds of a large bond loss.

ST.rationale: Momentum losses mark turbulent regimes with unstable cross-sectional pricing, which are associated with fatter tails.

FX.rationale: A strengthening dollar tightens global dollar funding and EM balance sheets, raising the probability of sharp EM and high-yield losses.

COM.rationale: Falling oil prices damage energy-heavy high-yield and oil-exporter sovereign credit, a known channel for tail losses.

MC.rationale: Financial stress combined with deteriorating labour-market news signals a recessionary credit shock, the main source of large default-driven losses.

ENDG.rationale: Recent poor returns tend to persist in illiquid credit indices because of slow price adjustment and redemption-driven selling, so losses cluster.

IR.rationale: Falling intermediate yields generate duration gains and easier funding, which supports large rallies in EM and high-yield bonds.

B.rationale: Tightening spreads with strong junk returns mark a credit relief rally that tends to continue in slow-adjusting bond markets.

V.rationale: Large gains cluster after volatility spikes, when risk premia are elevated and rebounds are sharp.

AP.rationale: Strong equity returns lead credit, so equity rallies precede large high-yield and EM bond gains.

ST.rationale: Momentum crashes coincide with violent rebounds of distressed, high-beta assets such as junk credit.

FX.rationale: A weakening dollar eases global funding conditions and EM balance sheets, favouring strong EM and high-yield returns.

COM.rationale: Oil rallies lift energy high-yield issuers and oil-exporting sovereigns sharply.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions mean high required returns, so the largest gains tend to occur as stressed conditions begin to ease.

ENDG.rationale: Positive short-horizon autocorrelation in credit index returns makes strong recent performance predictive of further large gains.
